title: Beyond a Welcome Sign
title_ja: 歓迎の看板のその先へ
fact_notes: 都市の施策と住民の事例は架空。異文化間対話と参加についての一般的教材。
英文・和訳・設問・解説は独自制作。

sentences.en: A small city announces that it wants to welcome more people who have moved from other countries.
sentences.ja: ある小さな都市が外国から移り住んだ人々をもっと歓迎したいと発表します。

sentences.en: The mayor suggests putting colorful welcome signs in several languages near the main railway station.
sentences.ja: 市長は中心駅の近くに複数の言語による色鮮やかな歓迎の看板を置くことを提案します。

sentences.en: Many residents like the idea because the signs could help visitors feel noticed rather than ignored.
sentences.ja: 看板が来訪者を無視されていないと感じさせる可能性があるため、多くの住民は賛成します。

sentences.en: However, a family that recently moved to the city explains that signs alone will not solve its greatest difficulties.
sentences.ja: しかし最近移住した家族は、看板だけでは最も大きな困難は解決しないと説明します。

sentences.en: The parents can understand some Japanese but find official school letters and public-service instructions difficult to follow.
sentences.ja: 親は日本語を少し理解できますが、学校の正式な手紙や行政サービスの案内は理解しにくいのです。

sentences.en: The discussion changes from how the city looks to how people actually obtain necessary information.
sentences.ja: 議論は町の見た目から、人々が実際に必要な情報を得る方法へ変わります。

sentences.en: A public message is useful only when its intended readers can understand what they need to do.
sentences.ja: 公的な案内は対象の読者が何をすべきか理解できるときに初めて役立ちます。

sentences.en: For example, a notice about an emergency shelter may include important details about its location and opening conditions.
sentences.ja: 例えば緊急避難場所の案内には、場所や利用条件について重要な細部が含まれるかもしれません。

sentences.en: If the wording is confusing, even a person who recognizes most of the words might misunderstand the instructions.
sentences.ja: 言い回しがわかりにくければ、多くの単語を知っている人でも指示を誤解するかもしれません。

sentences.en: The city therefore asks teachers and community volunteers to examine which kinds of messages cause the most difficulty.
sentences.ja: そこで市は教師や地域のボランティアに、どの種類の案内が最も難しいか調べるよう依頼します。

sentences.en: They discover that people do not all need the same type of support, even when they share a similar language background.
sentences.ja: 同じような言語的背景でも、全員が同じ支援を必要とするわけではないと気づきます。

sentences.en: Some want written translations, while others prefer clear explanations supported by pictures and opportunities to ask questions.
sentences.ja: 書面の翻訳を望む人もいれば、絵や質問の機会を伴うわかりやすい説明を好む人もいます。

sentences.en: The city first considers translating every notice into as many languages as possible without changing the original text.
sentences.ja: 市は最初、元の文章を変えずに可能な限り多くの言語へすべての案内を訳すことを考えます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, long and complicated sentences can remain difficult even after they have been translated accurately.
sentences.ja: それでも長く複雑な文は正確に訳しても難しいままの場合があります。

sentences.en: A volunteer suggests rewriting the original instructions in plain language before producing versions for other readers.
sentences.ja: あるボランティアは他の読者向けの版を作る前に、元の指示をやさしい言葉に書き直すことを提案します。

sentences.en: The team tests this idea by asking several residents to explain the steps that they would take after reading a notice.
sentences.ja: 担当者は住民数人に、案内を読んだ後に取る行動を説明してもらい、この案を試します。

sentences.en: Instead of judging success by the number of translated pages, they examine whether readers can identify the actions required.
sentences.ja: 翻訳ページ数で成功を判断するのではなく、読者が必要な行動を特定できるかを調べます。

sentences.en: Their results suggest that communication quality depends on clarity, useful context, and the chance to ask for help.
sentences.ja: その結果は、意思疎通の質が明確さ、役立つ文脈、助けを求める機会に左右されることを示します。

sentences.en: Another resident raises a concern about treating all newcomers as people who constantly require assistance from others.
sentences.ja: 別の住民は、新しく来た人すべてをいつも他人の支援が必要な人とみなすことに懸念を示します。

sentences.en: People who have recently arrived may also offer experience, ideas, and languages that improve the wider community.
sentences.ja: 最近来た人々も地域全体を良くする経験や考え、言語を提供できるかもしれません。

sentences.en: The city therefore invites them to help design information services rather than only receive the finished products.
sentences.ja: そこで市は完成品を受け取るだけでなく、情報サービスの設計に協力してもらうよう招きます。

sentences.en: Participants describe which parts of the existing system already work well and which steps create unnecessary barriers.
sentences.ja: 参加者は現在の仕組みのどこがすでに機能しており、どの段階が不要な障壁を生むか説明します。

sentences.en: Some suggestions concern language, while others involve office hours, transport routes, or the location of service desks.
sentences.ja: 提案には言語のほか、窓口時間、交通経路、サービス窓口の場所に関するものもあります。

sentences.en: These conversations reveal that welcoming people involves access and participation, not merely positive words on a sign.
sentences.ja: こうした対話は、人を歓迎するには看板の前向きな言葉だけでなく、利用と参加の機会が必要だと明らかにします。

sentences.en: After several months, the city opens an information desk that uses clear Japanese, selected translations, and simple visual guides.
sentences.ja: 数か月後、市はわかりやすい日本語、選ばれた翻訳、簡単な図を使う案内窓口を開きます。

sentences.en: It also invites residents to report when a message remains difficult to understand or when an important language is missing.
sentences.ja: 案内がなお理解しにくいときや重要な言語が欠けているときに知らせるよう住民にも呼びかけます。

sentences.en: As a result, the welcome signs become only the visible beginning of a larger effort to make services easier to use.
sentences.ja: その結果、歓迎看板はサービスを使いやすくする大きな努力の目に見える始まりにすぎないものとなります。

sentences.en: The city does not claim to have solved every problem, and it plans to review the project as needs change.
sentences.ja: 市はすべての問題を解決したとは主張せず、必要の変化に応じて事業を見直す予定です。

sentences.en: A genuine welcome is shown not only by what an institution says, but also by whether different people can understand and influence it.
sentences.ja: 本当の歓迎は組織が言うことだけでなく、異なる人々が理解し影響を与えられるかによっても示されます。

sentences.en: The most meaningful message may be an invitation to participate in shaping the community rather than simply entering it.
sentences.ja: 最も意味あるメッセージは、ただ地域に入るだけでなく地域づくりに参加してほしいという招待かもしれません。

questions.prompt: Why do many residents support multilingual signs?
options: They could help newcomers feel acknowledged.
They would eliminate all public services.
They would replace every school.
They would make transport free.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の「しかし最近移住した家族は、看板だけでは最も大きな困難は解決しないと説明します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What difficulty does the newly arrived family describe?
options: Finding the railway station.
Buying enough colorful signs.
Learning the city's name.
Understanding official letters and service instructions.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の「親は日本語を少し理解できますが、学校の正式な手紙や行政サービスの案内は理解しにくいのです。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why can a notice be difficult despite familiar words?
options: All emergencies are identical.
Every translation is incorrect.
Its wording may make the required action unclear.
A notice never has an intended reader.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「言い回しがわかりにくければ、多くの単語を知っている人でも指示を誤解するかもしれません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What kinds of support do different residents prefer?
options: Only visitors need clear information.
Some prefer translations and others pictures with explanations.
All people request exactly the same language service.
Everyone refuses written information.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「書面の翻訳を望む人もいれば、絵や質問の機会を伴うわかりやすい説明を好む人もいます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is the weakness of translating difficult sentences unchanged?
options: They may remain hard to understand.
The number of languages always decreases.
Translation removes the need for any testing.
Short messages always lose their meaning.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「それでも長く複雑な文は正確に訳しても難しいままの場合があります。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does the team test its revised instructions?
options: Count the number of colored signs.
Ask workers to guess which language is most popular.
Print more pages without speaking to readers.
Ask readers to describe what actions they would take.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「翻訳ページ数で成功を判断するのではなく、読者が必要な行動を特定できるかを調べます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What concern is raised about newcomers?
options: Every newcomer needs the same service.
People should never move between countries.
They should not be seen only as people needing help.
Newcomers cannot offer useful ideas.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「最近来た人々も地域全体を良くする経験や考え、言語を提供できるかもしれません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why are newcomers involved in design?
options: Existing residents have no useful knowledge.
Their experience can reveal barriers and useful improvements.
They must approve every national law.
Only recent arrivals can read signs.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「そこで市は完成品を受け取るだけでなく、情報サービスの設計に協力してもらうよう招きます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the city do after several months?
options: Open an information desk and invite feedback on unclear messages.
Remove all translations.
Declare that every difficulty has ended.
Replace teachers with signs.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落の「その結果、歓迎看板はサービスを使いやすくする大きな努力の目に見える始まりにすぎないものとなります。」が根拠です。

options: Multilingual signs alone solve every difficulty.
Visitors should not influence their communities.
A city's appearance matters more than its services.
A genuine welcome requires understandable services and meaningful participation.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落の「最も意味あるメッセージは、ただ地域に入るだけでなく地域づくりに参加してほしいという招待かもしれません。」が根拠です。

grammar.focus: but find official school letters and public-service instructions difficult to follow
grammar.explanation_ja: butは日本語の基本理解と公的文書の困難を対比します。

grammar.focus: even a person who recognizes most of the words might misunderstand
grammar.explanation_ja: evenは意外な場合を強調します。

grammar.focus: Instead of judging success by the number of translated pages
grammar.explanation_ja: instead of + 動名詞で評価方法の転換を示します。

grammar.focus: not only by what an institution says, but also by whether different people can understand and influence it
grammar.explanation_ja: not only A but also Bで歓迎の条件を広げます。

discourse.role_ja: 看板への期待と情報を理解する困難を対比します。
緊急避難所の案内を例示します。
正確な翻訳にも難しさが残ると示します。
看板がより広いサービス改善の始まりになる結果を示します。

paraphrases.source: The discussion changes from how the city looks to how people actually obtain necessary information.
paraphrases.rewrite: The debate shifts from appearance to practical access to information.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 見た目から必要情報へのアクセスに論点が移ることです。

paraphrases.source: They discover that people do not all need the same type of support, even when they share a similar language background.
paraphrases.rewrite: People with similar language backgrounds do not always need identical support.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同じ言語的背景でも必要な支援が異なるという意味です。

paraphrases.source: These conversations reveal that welcoming people involves access and participation, not merely positive words on a sign.
paraphrases.rewrite: Welcoming newcomers means enabling access and participation, not merely offering friendly words.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 友好的な言葉だけでなく参加の機会が必要という意味です。

paraphrases.source: The most meaningful message may be an invitation to participate in shaping the community rather than simply entering it.
paraphrases.rewrite: The deepest welcome invites people to help shape the community.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 地域づくりへの参加を促すことが大切という結論です。
